A very pleasant evening was spent at Southfields on July 2nd, when we met Kensington Argyll A.C. We had an easy win and outstanding recollections are of Alf. Orton winning the 880 yards handicap, our Walking Hon.
Wooderson, with Len Marchant 3rd and Alf Orton 4th. Bill Lucas won the mile, and Shrubb was 3rd.
He congratulates the team on their recent successes. Alf. Orton.—Now a Corporal in the R.A.F., Middle East, where he arrived after a monotonous two months' voyage.

Alf Orton, acknowledging the Xmas Card and the last Gazette, from the Middle East says: "They certainly brought back many happy memories." He says that after 8½ months in the desert he can now get into Cairo whenever he feels like it, and recently spent 7 days leave in Alexandria.

In a letter he sent he gave vivid details of house to house fighting in Italy with the London Irish Rifles. Alf Orton is still keeping fit in the desert, and hopes to be at the Hall very soon. Don Abbott is now with the R.A.F. in India.

Cook did well to gain second place in the Junior 220, and Alf Orton showed something like his old form in winning the 880 Yards event. Bob Wise ran well in the Senior 440 Yards, and Len Bishop took third place in the 1 Mile with Micky Walker, having a change from marathon running, close behind him.
Platt put in a good finish to gain second place, with Alf Orton third.

Jack Frost ran second in the 100 Yards, and also finished third in the 220, which was won by Teddy Read. Syd Jarlett and Bob Wise finished second and third in the 440, and Len Marchant won the 880 Yards, with Alf Orton fourth.
Morris, the Police champion, won the 880 Yards and Alf Orton ran well to credit us with third place. Rene Howell gained us first place in the 1 Mile and V.
Hartley of L.A.C. in the 440 Yards race, and Alf Orton did well to gain third place in the 880 event. Rene Howell won the 1 Mile for the Poly but only after a great race with V.

In the mile handicap a good crowd turned out and after Jack Brown looked like running through the field, he was held off on the final lap by Alf Orton who used his head as well as his legs. Placings: 1, A.
Alf Orton says that after 8 1/2 months in the desert he can now get in to Cairo. Hasn't felt like training; though a 2:06 time for 800 metres has nearly made him change his mind.
